title: Raghoram @ Ram Sagar v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Pankaj Naqvi, J.; Piyush Agrawal, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; bill challenge relegated to clause 6.5.
headnote: A writ challenging the correctness of an electricity bill is not maintainable when clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 affords a statutory, alternative and efficacious remedy. Counsel for the consumer being unable to controvert that remedy, the petition was dismissed on that ground alone.
facts: Raghoram @ Ram Sagar filed Writ-C No. 63 of 2021 in the Allahabad High Court against the State of Uttar Pradesh and three others, seeking to challenge the correctness of an electricity bill. Counsel for the petitioner, counsel for respondent nos. 2 to 4, and the Standing Counsel for the State were heard. The petitioner's counsel did not dispute that a statutory alternative remedy under the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 was available against the bill.

holding_units.holding: A writ petition challenging the correctness of an electricity bill is dismissed where clause 6.5 of the Uttar Pradesh Electricity Supply Code, 2005 provides a statutory, alternative and efficacious remedy which the petitioner does not controvert.

principle_tags.application: The writ against bill correctness was dismissed because clause 6.5 is a statutory, alternative and efficacious remedy.
Clause 6.5 was treated as the statutory remedy for a consumer disputing the correctness of an electricity bill.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the disputed electricity bill
not_decided.note: Merits of the bill were not examined; the petitioner was left to clause 6.5.
